newsitem.title: USA: Crop Growers execs acquitted in Espy-related trial.
newsitem.headline: Crop Growers execs acquitted in Espy-related trial.

text.p: Two formers executives of Crop Growers Corp, the nation's second largest crop insurance company, were found not guilty on Thursday of charges that they funnelled illegal corporate campaign contributions to the brother of former Agriculture Secretary Mike Espy in order to gain favor with the Clinton cabinet member.

The acquittal of former Crop Growers chairman John Hemmingson and of senior vice president Gary Black were the first major setbacks dealt to the criminal investigation of Espy that is being led by Independent Counsel Donald Smaltz.
Smaltz said in a statement that he was disappointed in the jury's verdict, and that he would "now move on to other aspects of our investigation."

Hemmingson and Black had been accused of defrauding the U.S. government by concealing more than $40,000 in corporate contributions to Henry Espy, in order to win the favor of Mike Espy and fatten their wallets.
Defense attorneys argued that the government's case lacked proof, and that the two former insurance executives acted in "good faith" that they were not doing anything wrong.

Hemmingson has already been found guilty in a separate trial in New Orleans of money laundering a $20,000 political contribution to Henry Espy, and last month the corporation of Crop Growers pleaded no contest to conspiring to defraud the Federal Election Commission and was fined $2 million.
Mike Espy has been under investigation since 1994 of accepting illegal gifts and favors while he was Secretary of Agriculture from companies his department regulated.

Smaltz's aggressive investigation has yielded impressive results up to this point. The probe has brought criminal indictments and charges against more than a dozen individuals and concerns and has resulted in the conviction of the largest fruit cooperative in the nation for fraud and illegal gratuities to Mike Espy.
The probe has been widely expected to lead to the indictment this year of the former Clinton cabient member.

Government investigators have also focused on the relationship between Espy and Tyson Foods Inc, the Arkansas-based poultry giant, and legal experts said an indictment of the poultry company is not unlikely.
